verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Every clause is stated, but as the paper's own two-step chain rather than as one display, and with the paper's X = ∞ encoded as an exterior radius. (a) The first equality (M,J,S)_f = (M,J,S)_0 is ModulatedProfileAssembly.Witness.exterior_{mass,transport,energy} for all X beyond the repair patch; the paper evaluates the same equality at X = ∞. (b) The second equality (M,J,S)_0(∞) = (0,0,0) is the mass_zero, transport_zero, energy_zero fields of the FiveMomentCertificate supplied by NominalProfile.Witness.five_moments, as integrals over Ioi 0; the integrands match term by term (M = ∫U, J = ∫U√(2x)E = ∫UH, S = ∫(U²−E²/2)). (c) For the modified (rather than modulated) layer, AssembledSlowBase.modified_mass_zero states M_f = 0 directly at the outer radius; since U_f vanishes beyond that radius, M_f is constant there and equals M_f(∞). (d) The angular half ∫_0^∞(H_f−H_0)dX = I_f(Y_1)−I_0(Y_1) = 0 appears as exterior_angular, I_f(X) = I_0(X) for X beyond the patch: I is the primitive of H, and H_f = H_0 outside the patch, so the two statements are interchangeable by the fundamental theorem of calculus. Lean states the single-profile angular moment only in the renormalized form ∫(√(2x)E − powerH) = 0 (the unrenormalized ∫H diverges), which is why the paper too writes this clause as a difference of two profiles.
